title: 999 or 111? Getting the right help with arthritis and frailty (UK)
meta_title: 999 or 111? Getting the right help with arthritis and frailty
meta_description: When to call 999, NHS 111 or your GP if you have arthritis and frailty: emergencies, urgent problems, hot swollen joints, falls and what to have ready.
excerpt: When to call 999, NHS 111 or your GP if you have arthritis and frailty: emergencies, urgent problems, hot swollen joints, falls and what to have ready.
direct_answer: Call 999 for life-threatening emergencies such as chest pain, stroke signs, severe breathing problems or serious injury. Use NHS 111 for urgent problems that are not emergencies. Contact your GP for ongoing or non-urgent issues.
author: Louis Maxwell

content:
Knowing who to call can save time and stress.

This guide explains the options. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Call 999 for

  • Chest pain.
  • Signs of stroke.
  • Severe breathing difficulty.
  • Serious injury or a fall where you cannot get up.

Use NHS 111 for

  • Urgent advice when unsure.
  • A single hot, swollen, very painful joint, especially with fever.
  • Out-of-hours problems.

Contact your GP for

Ongoing pain, flares and medicine questions.

Have ready

  • Medicines list.
  • Conditions list.
  • Contacts.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can a carer call 111 for me?

Yes.

Is 111 available online?

Yes, in England via 111.nhs.uk.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: When to call 999
  • NHS: When to use 111

Educational information for people in the United Kingdom — not a diagnosis or personal medical advice. Charity no. 1218461. Reviewed by Louis Maxwell (HCPC PH128483). Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
